subject: Contract evolution: capacity swap + temporary rate shelter
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroracommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Contract evolution: capacity swap + temporary rate shelter

Samir —

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Based on Aurora's Q3 forecast and the capacity pressure you signaled, we'd like to propose a short, pragmatic path to keep you protected on unit economics while you scale:

Proposal headline (high level)
- Move up to 20% of your current committed capacity into a labelled "burst pool" for 6 months (no change to overall committed quantity). This gives you flexible headroom without immediate commit change.
- In exchange Redwood provides a temporary rate shelter: a 6-month capped per-token rate that is 6–8% below current list for that burst pool, plus an operational credit equal to 50% of any overage billing in month 1 (to ease the ramp).
- At month 6 we'll run a true-up review with your team and recommend a steady-state commit that more closely matches observed run rate (no surprise retro billing beyond mutually agreed true-up).

Why we think this helps
- Aurora keeps predictable costs while avoiding an immediate long-term commit change.
- You get capacity elasticity to absorb campaign spikes.
- We get visibility on steady-state usage to recommend a better long-term commit and pricing band.

Ask
1) Can you share a brief Q3 daily average token forecast (attached template) by EOD Wed?
2) Would you be available to review legal-friendly wording (short amendment + MAP) Thurs or Fri this week?

I've attached a one-sheet forecast template to make the ask quick. If this is directionally acceptable I'll loop in Legal and Solutions to draft the MAP + amendment.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: Aurora_Forecast_Q3.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Samir Patel <samir@auroracommerce.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Lee <monica.lee@auroracommerce.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@auroracommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract evolution: capacity swap + temporary rate shelter

Jordan —

Appreciate the thoughtful approach. A few quick points from our side after an initial pass:

- Elasticity model: procurement is nervous about a "burst pool" with a lower rate unless there's a clear cap on how much of our baseline usage can be billed at that sheltered rate. Can you confirm the exact mechanics (e.g., first X tokens / day at sheltered rate, then standard)?
- Discount schedule: we were expecting something closer to a 10–12% anchoring for an upsell window given our expected run rate; 6–8% is directionally okay but procurement will push.
- Contract language: legal (Elena) wants the amendment to explicitly limit Redwood's right to materially change servicing regions or SLAs for the duration of the shelter.

I've attached our procurement questionnaire and a very high-level internal forecast. Monica (CC) will coordinate if we need to bring Procurement Ops into a call.

Can we do a short sync Wed 10am PT? If you can come with a worked example — e.g., 1-week scenario with tokens, rates, and resulting invoice — that would help.

Thanks,
Samir
VP Engineering, Aurora Commerce
samir@auroracommerce.com

Attachments: Procurement_Questionnaire_Aurora.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Contract evolution: capacity swap + temporary rate shelter (Aurora)

Team —

Pushing this thread over for quick alignment before Wed's call with Aurora (10am PT). High level: procurement pushed back on the rate anchor and wants explicit contract constraints. They also want a worked invoice example.

My proposal (internal):
- Offer a 6% sheltered per-token rate for the burst pool, with an explicit cap: the sheltered rate applies to up to 20% of monthly committed tokens and up to 1.5x of baseline daily volume for a 14-day spike window. Anything beyond that bills at standard committed overage rate.
- Provide a one-time operational credit equal to 50% of any overage in the first month (same as initial proposal).
- If Aurora increases steady-state usage by >25% at month 6, we offer a step-down discount (2% incremental discount on the new baseline for 12 months) to recognize scale.
- Legal language: short-term amendment + MAP with explicit region/SLA protection for the duration of the shelter.

Risks / asks for finance/legal:
- Need confirmation we can hold the 6% anchor without long-term exposure if Aurora stays elevated (i.e., we want the MAP to include a formal true-up and optional commit conversion).
- Can Finance build a worked example for Wed's call showing 3 scenarios: baseline, 14-day burst, and sustained uplift? I can send the forecast we got (Samir attached a small spreadsheet).

Attaching a draft SLA anchor (SLA_temp_anchor_v1.pdf) — please call out any clauses you think are necessary to meet Elena's ask.

-J

Attachments: SLA_temp_anchor_v1.pdf

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@auroracommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract evolution: capacity swap + temporary rate shelter — updated MAP and example

Samir / Monica / Elena —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per our discussion attached is a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a worked invoice example covering the three scenarios you requested (baseline / 14-day burst / sustained uplift). Summary of changes from my initial note:

Key updates
- Sheltered rate: final anchor set at 7% below current committed list for the burst pool (middle ground).
- Cap mechanics: sheltered rate applies to up to 20% of monthly committed tokens and up to 1.5x baseline daily average for a 14-day rolling window. Over that, standard overage rules apply.
- One-time operational credit: Redwood provides a 50% credit on first-month overage as promised.
- Scale incentive: if steady-state usage increases >25% at month 6 true-up, Aurora gets an incremental 2% discount on the new baseline for 12 months.
- Legal protection: short amendment locks region and baseline SLA levels for the 6-month shelter window; amendment is explicit that service region/SLA cannot be materially altered during that period.

Next steps (MAP)
1) Aurora: confirm Q3 daily-average forecast using the attached template (Samir sent a draft — thanks). Due: Fri 28 May EOD.
2) Redwood Solutions: finalize worked invoice scenarios and share by Thu EOD. (Ben taking point)
3) Legal: circulate amendment + short MAP for signature (Marissa to coordinate). Expected DocuSign link attached.
4) Execute amendment and enable burst pool (target activation: 3 business days after signature).

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/MAP-Aurora-DC-2027-0193

If this aligns, Elena — if you can sign off on the amendment language I'll send DocuSign to your procurement address.

Thanks all — appreciate the quick momentum.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: MAP_Aurora_v1.docx, worked_invoice_examples.pdf
